mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q01.stem: Match crimping-tool die shape to the terminal type used.
reasons: Combine the specified terminal with its compatible tool.
This statement is true. Combine the specified terminal with its compatible tool.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q02.stem: To keep measuring force constant, tighten as hard as possible every time.
reasons: This statement is false. Excessive force causes deformation and variation.
Excessive force causes deformation and variation.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q03.stem: Once current can be calculated, source capacity and resistor ratings no longer need checking.
reasons: This statement is false. Calculation and actual equipment suitability are separate checks.
Calculation and actual equipment suitability are separate checks.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q04.stem: If only a color change has been observed, do not report that the cause of burning is established.
reasons: Separate observations from inferred causes.
This statement is true. Separate observations from inferred causes.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q05.stem: A histogram always has time on its horizontal axis and monitors an upper control limit.
reasons: This statement is false. Its purpose differs from a time-ordered control chart.
Its purpose differs from a time-ordered control chart.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q06.stem: Across multiple drawing sheets, match components by following the same equipment identifiers and terminal numbers.
reasons: Check identification and cross-references.
This statement is true. Check identification and cross-references.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q07.stem: Matching resistance values allow differences in rated power and temperature to be ignored.
reasons: This statement is false. Check specifications beyond resistance value.
Check specifications beyond resistance value.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q08.stem: ESD precautions need be applied only after all work is finished.
reasons: This statement is false. Prevent exposure before handling begins.
Prevent exposure before handling begins.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q09.stem: A capacitor may retain charge after power-off.
reasons: Check residual energy and perform the specified treatment.
This statement is true. Check residual energy and perform the specified treatment.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q10.stem: Binary 1101 has exactly the same value as decimal 1101.
reasons: This statement is false. 8+4+0+1=13.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q11.stem: An explanation that power restoration alone will not restart equipment depends on assumptions such as a non-latching relay and a released start input.
reasons: Check circuit construction and input states.
This statement is true. Check circuit construction and input states.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q12.stem: Solar cells and storage batteries merely store unlimited electricity in the same way.
reasons: This statement is false. Do not confuse their roles because both names include cell or battery.
Do not confuse their roles because both names include cell or battery.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q13.stem: FRP electrical properties depend on factors such as glass versus carbon fiber.
reasons: Fiber, resin, orientation and content affect properties.
This statement is true. Fiber, resin, orientation and content affect properties.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q14.stem: A height gauge is used for heights from a reference plane and for marking out.
reasons: Match the dimension required to the instrument’s purpose.
This statement is true. Match the dimension required to the instrument’s purpose.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q15.stem: Positive charges always attract one another, while positive and negative charges always repel.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish force direction by charge signs.
Distinguish force direction by charge signs.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q16.stem: The fixed-item element of the three fixed rules includes deciding which item belongs at a designated location.
reasons: Make the item to be placed clear.
This statement is true. Make the item to be placed clear.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q17.stem: Check local exhaust conditions before chemical work.
reasons: Conditions must prevent vapor exposure.
This statement is true. Conditions must prevent vapor exposure.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q18.stem: Any old standard for any product can always be used unchanged within the same factory.
reasons: This statement is false. Check applicability and revision.
Check applicability and revision.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q19.stem: Before units, m and M always represent the same multiplier.
reasons: This statement is false. Record uppercase and lowercase correctly.
Record uppercase and lowercase correctly.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q20.stem: Do not determine current regulatory coverage from only the item count in old documents.
reasons: Check the regime’s date and applicable conditions.
This statement is true. Check the regime’s date and applicable conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q21.stem: LEDs and photodiodes only emit light in the same direction.
reasons: This statement is false. Distinguish light-related functions and arrow directions.
Distinguish light-related functions and arrow directions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q22.stem: Whether flux residue requires cleaning depends on material and product specifications.
reasons: Check type and process conditions.
This statement is true. Check type and process conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q23.stem: W and Wh are interchangeable expressions for the same quantity regardless of time.
reasons: This statement is false. Separate the rate of consumption from the total energy.
Separate the rate of consumption from the total energy.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q24.stem: FET gate drive and BJT base drive do not use the same terminal names and conditions.
reasons: Check the device type and data sheet.
This statement is true. Check the device type and data sheet.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q25.stem: x·0 always equals x, and x+1 always equals 0.
reasons: This statement is false. Apply the AND/OR laws for zero and one.
Apply the AND/OR laws for zero and one.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q26.stem: Reduction ratios for starting methods have assumptions about connections and equipment conditions.
reasons: Winding compatibility, protection and approval are needed.
This statement is true. Winding compatibility, protection and approval are needed.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q27.stem: Every PPM value always has the same number as the corresponding percentage.
reasons: This statement is false. The conversion factors differ.
The conversion factors differ.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q28.stem: The SI base unit of amount of substance is mol.
reasons: Distinguish mol from derived resistance units.
This statement is true. Distinguish mol from derived resistance units.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q29.stem: Checking component polarity or missing components and checking solder cracks examine different things.
reasons: Separate the different assembly-inspection items.
This statement is true. Separate the different assembly-inspection items.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-theory-q30.stem: Chamfering only means enlarging the entire hole diameter without limit.
reasons: This statement is false. Preserve required edge shape and dimensions.
Preserve required edge shape and dimensions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q01.stem: A tightening standard specifies 4 N·m, but the tool displays another unit. What should you do?
options: Check units, conversion and tool applicability before setting it.
Remove a washer to make tightening easier.
Tighten as much as possible by feel.
reasons: Torque is controlled by value and unit; do not leave a unit mismatch and copy the number.
Removing the washer changes the specified assembly and does not resolve units.
The number four in another unit may not equal 4 N·m.
Maximum tightening by feel risks excessive torque and broken parts.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q02.stem: You observe unusual equipment vibration. Which information should be central to the report?
options: Only criticism of the responsible person.
A decision to call it normal without records.
Equipment ID, time, operating state and observed vibration.
reasons: Criticism alone provides no equipment, timing or vibration conditions for investigation.
Presenting an uninvestigated cause as fact miscommunicates the situation.
Observed abnormality should not be declared normal without records.
Separate observed facts from inference and follow safety and reporting procedures.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q03.stem: A developed connection diagram shows coil K3 and contact K3 far apart. How should it be read?
options: Erase identifiers and wire by appearance.
Treat nearby K2 contacts as K3.
Trace operation using the corresponding equipment identifiers.
Assume they are unrelated because they are far apart.
reasons: Removing identifiers prevents tracing the correct coil/contact relationship.
Match identifiers, not proximity; do not relabel K2 as K3.
Coils and contacts may be drawn separately. Match equipment numbers and cross-references.
The same device may be separated in a developed diagram to make functions easier to follow.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q04.stem: An ideal transformer has 400 primary turns, 800 secondary turns and 24 V primary voltage. What is the secondary voltage?
reasons: Different turn counts mean the voltage ratio is not one.
Twice the turns gives twice the ideal voltage: 48 V. This ratio alone establishes neither capacity nor losses.
Adding turns does not produce a voltage; use the turns ratio.
This reverses the ratio; the secondary has more turns, so voltage rises.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q05.stem: A substitute transistor has its B, C and E terminals in a different order from the drawing. What should you do?
options: Ignore maximum ratings if the shape is similar.
Insert it in any orientation because it has three leads.
Verify terminal arrangement and rating compatibility in model documentation.
reasons: Matching shape does not prevent failure caused by insufficient maximum ratings.
B/C/E order can differ between three-lead device models.
B and E have different functions and cannot be swapped arbitrarily.
Three leads alone do not establish compatibility; compare both terminals and electrical conditions.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q06.stem: There are three relevant defects among 20000 shipped units. What is the PPM?
reasons: 15 results from multiplying the fraction by 100000 rather than a million.
1500 is ten times too high due to an incorrect conversion factor.
0.00015 is the fraction; multiply it by a million for PPM.
3/20000×1000000=150 PPM. Align case definitions and periods when comparing.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q07.stem: Under this app’s equally weighted practice scoring, theory is 20/30 and practical is 5/10. What is the section-by-section result?
options: Theory meets its threshold; practical does not, so there is no overall pass.
A total of 25 means a guaranteed pass.
Passing theory guarantees a pass regardless of practical.
reasons: The app requires at least 20/30 and 6/10 separately; practical 5/10 falls short. This does not guarantee unpublished official scoring or answer-count thresholds.
Separate practice thresholds do not allow a combined total to compensate for a shortfall.
Practical must independently reach at least 6/10.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q08.stem: You are preparing to crimp 2.0 mm² stranded wire, but the tool only states “2.0 mm solid wire.” What should happen before starting?
options: Use the blade because the numbers match.
Check the tool’s applicability to the stranded cross-section and terminal.
Crush the terminal with ordinary pliers.
Cut away half the conductor to make it thinner.
reasons: A solid-wire diameter marking is not the same application as stranded-wire area.
mm indicates diameter and mm² area; matching numbers do not establish compatibility. Check wire, terminal and tool together.
General pliers do not guarantee the specified crimp shape or force.
Cutting strands compromises the required area and connection performance.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q09.stem: After zeroing a dial indicator on a reference part, you compare another part’s deviation. What conditions are required?
options: Do not record the reference dimension if the pointer moves.
Contact a different surface obliquely each time.
Keep the reference surface, contact direction and probe displacement consistent.
Leave dirt on the surface plate.
reasons: Without a reference dimension, deviation cannot be related to actual size or specifications.
Changing direction or reference adds measurement differences beyond product differences.
Comparisons depend on reference and measuring posture. Changed conditions confound product and measurement differences.
Dirt changes the reference and posture, causing measurement error.

mfg1-electrical-mock-04-practical-q10.stem: A supplier presents an ISO certificate. What is the correct approach to product inspection?
options: Check certification scope and product requirements, then perform necessary inspections.
Abolish inspections without reading the scope.
reasons: Organizational certification differs from individual product conformity; compare scope and requirements separately.
The applicable revision matters when verifying requirements.
Certification does not automatically guarantee all individual products pass.
Abolishing inspections without reading the scope may violate contractual or product requirements.
